lines.cap: **Narrator:** This is Kavya. She is twelve. Her science teacher has given her a plant to keep alive all term.
**Kavya:** It's a plant. It doesn't DO anything. It just sits there. Being green.
**Narrator:** The plant has a name.
**Kavya:** It's called Plant.
**Narrator:** But this documentary is not about Kavya. It is about what Plant does all day. Which, it turns out, is a lot.
**Narrator:** Inside each leaf are millions of cells. And inside each cell are dozens of tiny green factories.
**Narrator:** This is one of them.
**Clive:** Hi. Clive. **Chloroplast**.
**Clive:** Not chloro-PHYLL. Chloro-PLAST. Chlorophyll is the green stuff. I'm the building it works in.
**Clive:** Every year, thousands of students mix us up. In exams. For marks.
**Narrator:** Clive's family has run on sunlight for a billion years.
**Clive:** And she says we don't do anything.
**Narrator:** Leaf Inc. Episode one: The Plant That Does Nothing.
**Narrator:** Seven a.m. Sunrise over Kavya's HDB block. Plant's working day begins.
**Clive:** Lights on, everyone! Phyllis! You're on!
**Phyllis:** Darling. Phyllis. **Chlorophyll**. The green **pigment**. I'm the reason this leaf looks fabulous.
**Clive:** Phyllis is chlorophyll. Millions of her work in here. All lead singers.
**Phyllis:** My job is to **absorb light energy**. Mostly **red** and **blue** light. Delicious.
**Kavya:** So it eats green light. That's why it's green.
**Phyllis:** Green? Yuck. No.
**Phyllis:** I **reflect** green light. It bounces back into your eyes. That's why leaves look green.
**Clive:** She rejects green, and then she wears it. That's Phyllis for you.
**Narrator:** **Photo** means light. **Synthesis** means making. **Photosynthesis**: making food, using light.
**Kavya:** I thought plants got their food from the soil.
**Clive:** Plants are **producers**: we make our own food. From the soil, we just take **water** and **minerals**.
**Clive:** We need **light**, **carbon dioxide** and **water**. Light's here. Where are the other two?
**Clive:** First, the tour. The leaf is **broad** and **flat**, to catch light, and **thin**, so gases don't travel far.
**Clive:** The roof: a **waxy cuticle**. Clear, to let light in. Waterproof, to keep water in.
**Clive:** Top floor: the **palisade** cells. Tall, packed with chloroplasts, and first to get the light. Most food is made here.
**Clive:** Downstairs: the **spongy** layer, with **air spaces**, so gases can reach every cell.
**Clive:** On the underside are the doors: tiny pores called **stomata**. One is a **stoma**.
**Clive:** Each stoma has two **guard cells**. They open and close it, controlling gas exchange and water loss.
**Clive:** They don't talk. They've never talked.
**Cosmo:** Hey. Cosmo. **Carbon dioxide**. From the air.
**Cosmo:** I don't walk in. I **diffuse**: from where there's **lots** of me, outside, to where there's **less**, inside.
**Cosmo:** And **diffusion** needs **no energy**. Which suits me.
**Dewi:** Coming through! Dewi! **Water**! Up from the ROOTS! Do you know how far that is?
**Dewi:** **Root hair cells** soaked me up from the soil. Then I came up the **xylem**: long, hollow tubes.
**Kavya:** Wait. How does water go UP?
**Dewi:** Water **evaporates** from the leaf, and that pulls more of us up. Like you, sucking a bubble tea straw.
**Clive:** It's called **transpiration**. Plant drinks bubble tea all day. Without the bubbles. Or the tea.
**Clive:** **Xylem** brings water in. **Phloem** carries sugar away. Both run in the **veins**.
**Clive:** Right. Phyllis: light energy, please. Cosmo, Dewi: in you go.
**Narrator:** Chlorophyll traps light energy, which joins carbon dioxide and water into a sugar: **glucose**.
**Gus:** Hiii! Gus! **Glucose**! Is this my first day? Is THIS my desk? I love it here!
**Clive:** Gus is glucose. The light energy is now stored in him, as **chemical energy**. A packed lunch, basically.
**Olive:** And then there's me. Olive. **Oxygen**. The **waste product**.
**Olive:** Nobody in here needs me. They open the stomata and put me out. Like the rubbish.
**Dewi:** Olive came out of ME, you know. Light energy splits **water**, and that's where oxygen comes from.
**Clive:** So: **carbon dioxide + water → glucose + oxygen**.
**Kavya:** **C**ars **W**on't **G**o **O**n **G**rass. Carbon dioxide, water, glucose, oxygen.
**Kavya:** So the ingredients are carbon dioxide, water... and sunlight?
**Clive:** No. Light isn't an ingredient. It's the **energy source**. Light and chlorophyll go **over the arrow**.
**Phyllis:** We're needed, darling, but never used up. I'm not an ingredient. I'm the talent.
**Clive:** The balanced **symbol equation**: **6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂**
**Cosmo:** Six of me...
**Dewi:** ...and six of me...
**Gus:** ...make just ONE of me? I'm so expensive!
**Clive:** Count them: **six** carbons, **twelve** hydrogens, **eighteen** oxygens, on each side. Forget the **sixes**, and it won't balance.
**Narrator:** Noon. Thousands of Guses have been made. Each one needs a job.
**Gus:** What's my job? Can I be a manager?
**Clive:** Four jobs. One: **respiration**. The mitochondria next door break glucose down to **release energy**. Nice guys. Very tired.
**Clive:** Yes, plants respire too. **All the time**, day and night. We only photosynthesise in the light.
**Clive:** Two: **storage**. Spare glucose is joined into **starch**, and stored in leaves, stems and seeds.
**Gus:** Ooh, it's me, holding hands with hundreds of me!
**Clive:** Starch is **insoluble**, so it doesn't upset the cell's water balance. Perfect for storage.
**Clive:** Three: **cellulose**, tough fibres for **cell walls**, so the plant can stand up straight.
**Clive:** Four: **proteins**, for growth. For those, we also need **nitrates** from the soil.
**Gus:** **R**eally **S**weet **C**runchy **P**lants! Respiration, starch, cellulose, proteins!
**Phyllis:** And to make me, darling, the plant needs **magnesium**.
**Phyllis:** Without it, leaves turn **yellow**: **chlorosis**. Less of me, less light absorbed, less food.
**Phyllis:** I don't want to talk about it.
**Narrator:** Last question: where does a growing plant's new mass come from? Most people say the soil.
**Cosmo:** It's me. Most of a plant's **dry mass** comes from **carbon dioxide** in the air.
**Cosmo:** Wood? Mostly me. Trees are basically made of thin air. You're welcome.
**Narrator:** Two p.m. Kavya wants Plant to photosynthesise faster.
**Kavya:** More light, more food, right? Here. Have my desk lamp. You're welcome.
**Narrator:** The rate of photosynthesis rises. And then it levels off.
**Kavya:** Why did it stop? Is it full?
**Clive:** We're not full. We're out of Cosmo. Light isn't holding us back now. **Carbon dioxide** is. In normal air, it often does.
**Narrator:** A **limiting factor** is whatever's in **shortest supply**. Increase it: the rate rises. Increase anything else: nothing.
**Clive:** On a graph, that flat bit is a **plateau**. It means **another factor** is now limiting.
**Kavya:** Three limiting factors. **L**ight **C**ools **T**hings: **light intensity**, **carbon dioxide concentration**, **temperature**.
**Kavya:** What if I put you by the aircon compressor? It's super hot there.
**Clive:** Warmer helps, up to a point. We run on **enzymes**. But above about **40 to 45 °C**, they **denature**.
**Clive:** Their shape is destroyed and the rate crashes. Please. Not the compressor.
**Narrator:** Seven p.m. Sunset. No light, so photosynthesis stops. Respiration carries on.
**Gus:** So at night, the plant only respires! It takes in **oxygen**, and gives out **carbon dioxide**!
**Clive:** By day, we photosynthesise **faster** than we respire. So overall, we take in **carbon dioxide** and give out **oxygen**.
**Narrator:** Photosynthesis **stores** energy in glucose. Respiration **releases** it. They're almost exact **opposites**.
**Narrator:** Friday. Kavya must prove Plant has been photosynthesising, by testing a leaf for **starch**.
**Narrator:** First, the plant is **destarched**: kept in the dark for a day or two, to use up old starch.
**Kavya:** Already done. By accident. It was in my wardrobe last weekend.
**Clive:** We remember.
**Kavya:** Then I covered part of one leaf with **foil**, so that bit got no light.
**Narrator:** Step one: **boil it in water**. That kills the leaf, and breaks down membranes so iodine can get in.
**Clive:** Not my leaf. That's Kevin's leaf. Kevin knew the risks.
**Narrator:** Step two: **boil it in ethanol**, to remove the green **chlorophyll**, so the colour change is easy to see.
**Phyllis:** They're removing ME? This is an outrage, darling!
**Kavya:** Ethanol is **flammable**. So the Bunsen goes **off**, and it's heated in a **water bath**.
**Narrator:** Step three: **warm water**, to soften it. Step four: **iodine solution**. Orange-brown turns **blue-black** where there's starch.
**Kavya:** **W**e **E**nd **W**ith **I**odine. Water, ethanol, warm water, iodine.
**Kavya:** Blue-black! Except under the foil. That bit stayed orange-brown. No light, no starch.
**Narrator:** On a green and white **variegated** leaf, only the green parts go blue-black: **chlorophyll** is needed. Remove carbon dioxide with **soda lime**: no starch.
**Kavya:** Conclusion. Plant does not do nothing.
**Narrator:** Photosynthesis starts nearly every **food chain**. If you're eating right now, it began as sunlight, caught by a leaf.
**Olive:** And the **oxygen** you're breathing? Made by photosynthesis. Plants, and plankton in the sea.
**Olive:** So really, I'm the main character.
**Clive:** She's going to be unbearable now.

chapters.title: The staff save you some marks

lines.cap: **Narrator:** Before the credits: exam advice from the staff of Plant.
**Clive:** One. **Chloroplast**: the structure. **Chlorophyll**: the green pigment inside it. Get our names right.
**Phyllis:** Two. Chlorophyll **reflects** green light, darling. It absorbs mainly **red** and **blue**.
**Cosmo:** Three. Light goes **over the arrow**, not in as a reactant. And keep the **sixes**.
**Olive:** Four. Photosynthesis takes **in** carbon dioxide and gives **out** oxygen. Not the other way round.
**Gus:** Five! Plants respire **all the time**! Not just at night!
**Dewi:** Six. A flat graph doesn't mean the plant is full. It means **another factor** is limiting.
**Kavya:** Seven. In the starch test, heat ethanol in a **water bath**, flame **off**.
**Narrator:** Leaf Inc. will return.
**Clive:** So. The Guards. Anything you'd like to add?
**The Guards:** ...Closed.
**Narrator:** The documentary crew is now locked inside the leaf until morning.
